synthesis:draft.headline: SA1 experienced a large high-price episode; peak 4,981 $/MWh (interval ending 2026-07-30T16:35:00Z / 2026-07-31 02:05 ACST).
summary: Peak 5-minute RRP observed 4,981 $/MWh at interval ending 2026-07-30T16:35:00Z (2026-07-31 02:05 ACST) (price timeline peak).
There were 214 five-minute intervals at-or-above the analysis threshold of 300 $/MWh during the window (event detector).
Dispatch TOTALDEMAND at the 5-minute peak interval was 1,472.82 MW; DISPATCH NETINTERCHANGE at that interval was -82.59 MW (net flow into SA1 / import).
The unweighted mean 5-minute RRP over the window was 416.71 $/MWh and the minimum sampled RRP in the window was 75.14288 $/MWh (price timeline).
AEMO published a market notice reporting a City West transformer trip and 275 kV circuit breaker trip on 30/07/2026 [c1].
Generator SCADA observations show a large negative change for SNAPPER1 of -148.38 MW in the 10:40→22:35 UTC window (descriptive SCADA observation).
Forecast vs actual operational demand for the 24 half-hours around the event: MAE = 32.88 MW, mean error = 4.88 MW (compare_forecast_actual).

possible_explanations.statement: A large change in generation SCADA for units such as SNAPPER1 may have contributed to tight local supply conditions around the evening peak (see SCADA change ev0940).
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Obtain unit-level bid/offer and availability/outage records plus dispatch messages for the specific 5-minute dispatch runs around 2026-07-30T16:35:00Z and compare the unit availability/bids to SCADA changes.

possible_explanations.statement: Interconnector flows being net into SA1 at the peak (DISPATCH NETINTERCHANGE −82.59 MW ev0438) might indicate constrained import capability or changing interconnector support that could be relevant.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Fetch interconnector availability, limit status and binding/instruction logs for the Heywood/Murraylink intervals around the peak and check for limit binding or sudden changes.

possible_explanations.statement: AEMO reported a City West transformer T_1 and breaker 6675 trip on 30/07/2026 which might be related to system conditions that day [c1].
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Align the transformer trip event timestamps and power system fault logs with dispatch 5-minute intervals, unit SCADA traces and rebid activity to test temporal correlation and influence.

possible_explanations.statement: Forecast vs actual demand errors were relatively small (MAE 32.88 MW ev1064), so large unexpected half-hourly demand forecast errors alone might be less likely to explain the extreme 5-minute RRP peak.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare 5-minute dispatch TOTALDEMAND (ev0437) and intra‑half‑hour ramps to the half-hour forecast/actual pairs to see if intra‑half‑hour demand dynamics differed from the half-hour forecasts.

Ancillary services (FCAS) activations, administered price cap or price override records for the 5-minute intervals were not retrieved.
Interconnector limit status and binding logs for the precise 5-minute intervals are not present here.
Detailed unit availability/outage notices for generator units during the peak interval are not included in the retrieved evidence.
missing_evidence: DISPATCHPRICE revision/audit rows (DISPATCH_PRICE_REVISION) and ROP/APC flags for 2026-07-30 16:20–16:40 UTC (to detect overrides or price capping).
